what_its_for: Sotagliflozin is used to lower the risk of serious heart problems, such as hospitalization for heart failure or death from heart-related causes, in adults who have heart failure or type 2 diabetes with kidney disease and other heart risk factors. It belongs to a class of medicines called SGLT inhibitors, which work by helping your kidneys remove extra sugar from your body through your urine, and also help reduce fluid buildup around your heart.
how_to_take: Take sotagliflozin by mouth, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Do not crush, chew, or break the tablet unless your doctor tells you it is okay.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 200 mg once daily. Your doctor may increase your dose to 400 mg once daily if your body tolerates the lower dose well. Always follow your doctor's instructions about your specific dose, as it may be different based on your kidney function and other health conditions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store sotagliflozin at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Store it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use any medicine past the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol, as it can increase your risk of low blood sugar and dehydration. Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first. Try to avoid becoming dehydrated — drink enough fluids, especially during hot weather or when you are sick with vomiting or diarrhea. Avoid genital area hygiene habits that could increase your risk of infection. Talk to your doctor before taking over-the-counter pain relievers like ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) or naproxen (Aleve), as these can affect your kidneys.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you notice: signs of a serious genital infection such as pain, redness, swelling, or a bad smell around your genitals or backside (this could be a rare but serious condition called Fournier's Gangrene); signs of a urinary tract infection such as burning when you urinate, needing to urinate very often, or blood in your urine; signs of low blood pressure such as dizziness, lightheadedness, or fainting; signs of low blood sugar such as shakiness, sweating, fast heartbeat, or confusion (especially if you take insulin or other diabetes medicines); unusual tiredness, trouble breathing, nausea, vomiting, or stomach pain (these could be signs of a serious condition called ketoacidosis, even if your blood sugar is not very high); or decreased urination or swelling in your legs, which could mean your kidneys are being affected.
when_it_works: Sotagliflozin starts working shortly after your first dose, but it may take several weeks to months before you notice the full benefits for your heart. Do not stop taking it even if you feel well, because it is working to protect your heart over time. Keep all follow-up appointments with your doctor so they can check how the medicine is working for you.
special_populations: Older adults (age 65 and over) may be more sensitive to side effects such as low blood pressure and dehydration, so extra monitoring may be needed. This medicine is not recommended for people with type 1 diabetes unless directed by a specialist. It should be used with caution in people with reduced kidney function, and your doctor will check your kidney function before and during treatment. Sotagliflozin should not be used if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as it may harm an unborn baby or nursing infant. Always tell your doctor about all medications, vitamins, and supplements you are taking before starting sotagliflozin.
